description: Eleventy framework layer: base Nunjucks layout plus a landing page in Markdown.

buildHints.whenToUse: Content-first static sites, blogs, documentation, or any project where pages are authored in Markdown and served as pre-rendered HTML with no client-side JS.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Eleventy serves on port 8097 with live-reload; the landing page renders from `src/index.md`.
Add new pages as `.md` or `.njk` files under `src/` — each file becomes a route. The base layout is at `src/_includes/base.njk`.
Run `pnpm build` to emit HTML to `_site/` — no server required, deploy anywhere (Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages).
Run `node validate-eleventy.mjs` to confirm the scaffold is wired correctly before pushing.
gotchas: Eleventy's `type: module` package uses ESM — `.eleventy.js` must use `export default` syntax, not `module.exports`.
Layout resolution uses `src/_includes/` because `.eleventy.js` sets `layouts: '_includes'`. If you move layouts, update both the config and all front-matter `layout:` references.
The `src/assets/` passthrough copy is configured but the directory is not created by default — run `mkdir -p src/assets` before adding static files or the passthrough silently no-ops.
`pnpm dev` starts a live-reload server via `--serve`; `pnpm build` does a one-shot build to `_site/` with no server.
architectureNotes: One layout for the whole site — `base.njk` is intentionally minimal. Add `src/_includes/post.njk` for blog-post-specific chrome and set `layout: post.njk` in those pages' front matter.
Global data files live in `src/_data/` — any `.json` or `.js` file there is accessible in every template by its filename (e.g., `src/_data/nav.json` → `{{ nav }}` in any template).

placeholders.description: Site header outputs `{{ headline }}` and `{{ subheadline }}`. After scaffold replacement these hold concrete strings; to override at runtime, add them to `src/_data/site.json`.
Landing page scaffold. Replace the body content and update the `title` front-matter key to match your project name.
